question: Should dispatchable exact-review backlog intentionally reduce the combined broad sweep and commit-review allowance to 16 workers when congested and 4 when saturated?
rationale: Tests can validate implementation mechanics, but deciding how aggressively one automation lane should preempt two other productive lanes requires maintainer ownership of the throughput tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt adaptive priority
options.body: Approve the 16/4 shared residual caps, contingent on a clean rebase and live throttle-and-recovery proof.

options.title: Use softer residual caps
options.body: Keep pressure-aware yielding but select higher limits after observing production queue, GitHub API, and publication capacity.

options.title: Keep lanes independent
options.body: Reject cross-lane preemption and address exact-review backlog only through exact-lane capacity and recovery improvements.

recommendation.title: Adopt adaptive priority
recommendation.body: Approve the 16/4 shared residual caps, contingent on a clean rebase and live throttle-and-recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged exact-review capacity and recovery change makes this person the strongest available owner for the cross-lane throughput decision.
